Source: Live Azure SQL Managed Instance measurements on ltrlab552754-mi, executed from ltrlab-vm by az vm run-command invoke.
LtrBackupAvailabilityDelayNote: LTR policy was set on mitest and the immediate LTR backup list returned no backups. No multi-day wait was performed.
TdeDecryptSizeBasis: ROWS file GiB from sys.database_files. Total file GiB, including LOG and FILESTREAM, is also preserved per measurement.
TdeDecryptNote: Two non-zero, non-degenerate points support a coarse two-point slope. R-squared is null because two points would make it tautological. Service-managed TDE was enabled by default before ALTER DATABASE SET ENCRYPTION OFF.
BackupToUrlNote: BACKUP DATABASE TO URL WITH COPY_ONLY, COMPRESSION was measured for the two TDE calibration databases after encryption was off and the DEK was dropped. R-squared is null because two points would be tautological.
MiPitrRestoreProxyNote: Same-instance PITR restore of mitest is an indicative lower-bound proxy for restore machinery. It is not an LTR restore measurement, and LTR restore may be slower because LTR backups can live in different storage.
MiBackupArtifactRestoreNote: This is a real RESTORE DATABASE from the COPY_ONLY .bak artifact into a new Managed Instance database with row count, aggregate checksum, and file allocation compared against the source. It is distinct from RESTORE VERIFYONLY and distinct from LTR restore.
MiBackupRestoreWithStatsNote: Initial RESTORE DATABASE attempt failed before artifact consumption because Managed Instance does not support RESTORE WITH STATS, Msg 41901. The same artifact restored successfully without STATS.
SqlDatabaseBacpacArtifactImportNote: Existing BACPAC artifact was downloaded from private blob storage to ltrlab-vm and imported with client-side sqlpackage using an Entra token from IMDS. az sql db import was not used. Row count, aggregate checksum, and file allocation were compared against the source.
SqlDatabaseBacpacImportRateNote: Only one BACPAC import size was measured in this task, so no import slope or regression is reported.
LtrRestoreNote: Managed Instance LTR restore is now measured, but at ONE size only, so no slope and no fixed term can be fitted. LtrRestoreMinPerGb and LtrRestoreFixedMin stay null deliberately. Do not substitute MiPitrRestoreProxy values as measured LTR restore constants, and do not derive a per-GiB rate from the single observation below.

LtrRestoreObservation.PrecisionNote: The database was absent from the listing at t0+17.2s and Online at t0+41.4s, so true completion lies in that interval. Only the upper bound is safe to quote as a worst case.

LtrRestoreDataIntactNote: Row count and aggregate checksum compared between the source database and the LTR-restored copy. This is a real restore from an LTR backup, distinct from RESTORE VERIFYONLY, distinct from PITR restore, and distinct from restoring the extracted .bak artifact.
LtrRestoreArrivesEncryptedNote: CRITICAL PLANNING FINDING. The LTR-restored database arrived with service-managed TDE active, encryption_state 3, encryptor_type CERTIFICATE, even though the source database had since had encryption turned off and its DEK dropped. The LTR backup preserves the encryption state at backup time, not the current state of the source. Every LTR-sourced restore in a real drain must therefore be decrypted before BACKUP TO URL will succeed, so the decrypt cost multiplies across every retained backup and is never a one-off.
LtrSourcedDrainNote: End-to-end drain executed from an LTR backup as the source: LTR restore, decrypt, drop DEK, BACKUP TO URL with COPY_ONLY and COMPRESSION, then RESTORE VERIFYONLY. This closes the last unproven link in the chain. Timings below are for a small database, 64 MiB ROWS, and must not be extrapolated as rates.
LtrSourcedDrainBlobVerificationNote: Blob existence and size confirmed by Blob REST list from ltrlab-vm inside the VNet, using an IMDS token for the user-assigned identity. Storage has allowSharedKeyAccess false and publicNetworkAccess Disabled, so listing from outside the VNet fails by design.
MiStopStartNote: A General Purpose managed instance CAN be stopped, which contradicts an earlier claim in this repository that it cannot. Tenant automation stopped this instance at 2026-09-10T21:41:17Z without warning. Compute and licensing charges stop while storage and backup charges continue. A stopped instance takes no automated backups and skipped LTR backups are never backfilled, so an instance must not be stopped during an LTR wait.
MiColdStartNote: Cold start from Stopped to Ready, measured 2026-09-11T07:10:54Z to approximately 07:31:27Z, polled at 60 to 90 second intervals. Budget roughly 20 minutes before any drain work can begin on a stopped instance.
MiStoppedInstanceLtrPolicyQueryTrapNote: While the instance was stopped, az sql midb ltr-policy show failed with LongTermRetentionPolicyNotSupported and the misleading text 'Database mitest does not exist on server'. The database and the policy were both intact; the same command returned P12W once the instance reached Ready. Do not interpret this error on a stopped instance as loss of LTR configuration.
